text:
The major product of the following reaction is:

[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 28th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The substrate is 3,5-dibromo-2-phenylheptane, $\mathrm{C}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{5}-\mathrm{CH}(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3})-\mathrm{CHBr}-\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}-\mathrm{CHBr}-\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}-\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}$ (C-1 is the methyl group on C-2). Excess alcoholic KOH on heating removes two molecules of HBr by E2 elimination.

The Br on C-3 is eliminated together with the benzylic H on C-2, giving the C-2=C-3 double bond, which is trisubstituted and conjugated with the benzene ring.

The Br on C-5 is eliminated together with an H on C-4, giving the C-4=C-5 double bond, conjugated with C-2=C-3.

The major product is therefore the fully conjugated $\mathrm{C}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{5}-\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3})=\mathrm{CH}-\mathrm{CH}=\mathrm{CH}-\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}-\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}$, 2-phenylhepta-2,4-diene. The isomer 6-phenylhepta-2,4-diene, $\mathrm{C}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{5}-\mathrm{CH}(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3})-\mathrm{CH}=\mathrm{CH}-\mathrm{CH}=\mathrm{CH}-\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}$, is also a conjugated diene, but its double bonds are not conjugated with the ring, so it is less stable.


[IMG]

Hence, the correct option is (C).

text:
Match List - I with List - II.
 
  
    List - I (Complex)
    List - II (Hybridisation of central metal ion)
  
  
    (A) [CoF$_{6}$]$^{3-}$
    $(I) d^{2}sp^{3}$
  
  
    (B) [NiCl$_{4}$]$^{2-}$
    $(II) sp^{3}$
  
  
    (C) [$Co(NH_{3})_{6}$]$^{3+}$
    (III$) sp^{3}d^{2}$
  
  
    (D) [$Ni(CN)_{4}$]$^{2-}$
    (IV) dsp$^{2}$
  
 Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 28th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Co ($Z=27$) is $[\text{Ar}]3d^{7}4s^{2}$, so $\mathrm{Co}{}^{3+}$ is $3d^{6}$; Ni ($Z=28$) is $[\text{Ar}]3d^{8}4s^{2}$, so $\mathrm{Ni}{}^{2+}$ is $3d^{8}$. The $4s$ electrons are removed first.

(A) $[\mathrm{CoF}{}_{6}]{}^{3-}$: $\mathrm{F}{}^{-}$ is a weak field ligand, so the $3d^{6}$ electrons are not paired (4 unpaired electrons) and the outer $4s$, $4p$ and $4d$ orbitals are used: $sp^{3}d^{2}$, matching (III).


[IMG]

(B) $[\mathrm{NiCl}{}_{4}]{}^{2-}$: $\mathrm{Cl}{}^{-}$ is a weak field ligand, so no pairing occurs (2 unpaired electrons) and the $4s$ and three $4p$ orbitals are used: $sp^{3}$, tetrahedral, matching (II).


[IMG]

(C) $[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}{}_{3}){}_{6}]{}^{3+}$: $\mathrm{NH}{}_{3}$ pairs the six $3d$ electrons into three orbitals, leaving two $3d$ orbitals vacant: $d^{2}sp^{3}$, inner orbital complex, matching (I).


[IMG]

(D) $[\mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{CN}){}_{4}]{}^{2-}$: $\mathrm{CN}{}^{-}$ is a strong field ligand, so the eight $3d$ electrons pair into four orbitals, leaving one $3d$ orbital vacant: $dsp^{2}$, square planar, matching (IV).


[IMG]

The matching is (A)-(III), (B)-(II), (C)-(I), (D)-(IV).

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 28th January Evening Shift

text:
Which of the following is/are not correct with respect to energy of atomic orbitals of hydrogen atom?
(A) 1s (B) 1s (C) 1s (D) 1s < 2s < 4s < 3d
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 28th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In the hydrogen atom the energy of an orbital depends only on $n$, $E_{n}=-\dfrac{13.6}{n^{2}}\text{eV}$, so all orbitals of one shell have the same energy:

$1s<2s=2p<3s=3p=3d<4s=4p=4d=4f$

(A) $1s<2p<3d<4s$ follows $n=1,2,3,4$ in increasing order, so it is correct.

(B) $1s<2s=2p<3s=3p$ is correct, since $2s$ and $2p$, and $3s$ and $3p$, share the same $n$.

(C) $2s<2p$ is not correct, because $2s$ and $2p$ have equal energy in hydrogen.

(D) $4s<3d$ is not correct, because $3d$ ($n=3$) lies below $4s$ ($n=4$); the order $4s<3d$ applies only to multi-electron atoms.

Statements (C) and (D) are not correct.

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 28th January Evening Shift

text: The amphoteric oxide among $\mathrm{V}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{3},\mathrm{V}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{4}$ and $\mathrm{V}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{5}$, upon reaction with alkali leads to formation of an oxide anion. The oxidation state of V in the oxide anion is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 28th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Among the vanadium oxides the acidic character rises with the oxidation state: $\mathrm{V}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}{}_{3}$ (+3) is basic, $\mathrm{V}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}{}_{4}$ (+4) is less basic and dissolves in acids to give $\mathrm{VO}{}^{2+}$ salts, and $\mathrm{V}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}{}_{5}$ (+5) is amphoteric, though mainly acidic.

With alkali, $\mathrm{V}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}{}_{5}$ gives the vanadate ion:

$\mathrm{V}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}{}_{5}+6\mathrm{OH}{}^{-}\longrightarrow 2\mathrm{VO}{}_{4}{}^{3-}+3\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}$

In $\mathrm{VO}{}_{4}{}^{3-}$, $x+4(-2)=-3$, so $x=+5$.

Hence, the correct option is (B).

text:
The total number of compounds from below when treated with hot KMnO$_{4}$, giving benzoic acid is:

[IMG]

[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 28th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Hot $\mathrm{KMnO}{}_{4}$ oxidises an alkyl side chain on a benzene ring to $-\mathrm{COOH}$ at the ring carbon, whatever the chain length, provided the benzylic carbon carries at least one H.

Toluene, ethylbenzene, isopropylbenzene, isobutylbenzene $\mathrm{C}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{5}\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{CH}(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}){}_{2}$ and propylbenzene each have benzylic H, so each gives $\mathrm{C}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{5}\mathrm{COOH}$: 5 compounds.


[IMG]

tert-Butylbenzene and 2-phenylpropan-2-ol, $\mathrm{C}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{5}\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{OH})(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}){}_{2}$, have no benzylic H, so their side chains are not oxidised.

4,4'-Dimethylbiphenyl has benzylic H, but each $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}$ is oxidised to $\mathrm{COOH}$ while the ring–ring bond is untouched, so it gives biphenyl-4,4'-dicarboxylic acid, not benzoic acid.

Hence, the correct option is (C).

text:
The purification method based on the following physical transformation is :
$\text{Solid}_{(X)}\leftarrow ^{\text{Heat}}\text{Vapour}_{(X)}\leftarrow ^{\text{Cool}}\text{Solid}_{(X)}$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 28th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The purification method described by the transformation:

$\text{Solid}_{(X)}\leftarrow ^{\text{Heat}}\text{Vapour}_{(X)}\leftarrow ^{\text{Cool}}\text{Solid}_{(X)}$

is known as Sublimation.

In sublimation, a solid substance directly transforms into its gaseous phase upon heating and reverts back to the solid phase upon cooling. This technique is commonly used to purify substances, particularly those that sublime more easily than others under the same conditions. Sublimation is effective for separating substances with different volatility, like separating ammonium chloride from a mixture with sodium chloride, as ammonium chloride sublimates while sodium chloride does not.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 28th January Evening Shift

text:
Identify the inorganic sulphides that are yellow in colour :
(A) $(NH_{4})_{2}S$
(B) $PbS$
(C) $CuS$
(D) $As_{2}S_{3}$
(E) $As_{2}S_{5}$
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 28th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
We want to identify which among the listed sulfides are yellow in color:

$\mathbf{(}𝐍𝐇_{𝟒}\mathbf{)}_{𝟐}𝐒$  

Ammonium sulfide is typically encountered as an aqueous solution that can be colorless to slightly yellowish in solution form. It is not known as a distinct “yellow sulfide” compound in the same sense as solid colored sulfides like orpiment (see below).  

$𝐏𝐛𝐒$ (lead(II) sulfide)  

$\text{PbS}$ (Galena) is well-known to be black or grayish‐black in color.

$𝐂𝐮𝐒$ (copper(II) sulfide)  

$\text{CuS}$ is black (covellite).

$𝐀𝐬_{𝟐}𝐒_{𝟑}$ (arsenic(III) sulfide)  

$\text{As}_{2}\text{S}_{3}$ (orpiment) is characteristically yellow.

$𝐀𝐬_{𝟐}𝐒_{𝟓}$ (arsenic(V) sulfide)  

$\text{As}_{2}\text{S}_{5}$ is also typically a yellow sulfide.

Hence, among the options given,

$\mathbf{(}𝐃\mathbf{)}As_{2}S_{3}$ and

$\mathbf{(}𝐄\mathbf{)}As_{2}S_{5}$

are the two yellow inorganic sulfides.  

Correct Choice
$\text{(D) and (E) only.}$

text:
Consider an elementary reaction

$\mathrm{A}(\mathrm{g})+\mathrm{B}(\mathrm{g})\to \mathrm{C}(\mathrm{g})+\mathrm{D}(\mathrm{g})$

If the volume of reaction mixture is suddenly reduced to $\frac{1}{3}$ of its initial volume, the reaction rate will become '$x$' times of the original reaction rate. The value of $x$ is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 28th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For an elementary reaction the rate law follows the stoichiometry:

$\text{rate}=k[\mathrm{A}][\mathrm{B}]=k\dfrac{n_{\mathrm{A}}}{V}\cdot \dfrac{n_{\mathrm{B}}}{V}$

When the volume is suddenly reduced to $\dfrac{V}{3}$, the moles are unchanged, so each concentration becomes 3 times:

$\text{rate}^{'}=k\dfrac{3n_{\mathrm{A}}}{V}\cdot \dfrac{3n_{\mathrm{B}}}{V}=9\times \text{rate}$

So $x=9$.

Hence, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 28th January Evening Shift

text: The spin only magnetic moment ( $μ$ ) value (B.M.) of the compound with strongest oxidising power among $\mathrm{Mn}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{3},\mathrm{TiO}$ and VO is $____________ B.M. ($Nearest integer).
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 28th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The compound with the strongest oxidizing power among Mn₂O₃, TiO, and VO is Mn₂O₃. This conclusion is based on the standard electrode potential ($E^{\circ }$) value:

$E_{\text{Mn}^{+3}/\text{Mn}^{+2}}^{\circ }=+1.57\text{V}$

For Mn³⁺, the electronic configuration is $d^{4}$. The spin-only magnetic moment ($μ$) is calculated as follows:

$μ=\sqrt{n(n+2)}\text{BM}$

Where $n$ is the number of unpaired electrons. Here, $n=4$:

$μ=\sqrt{4(4+2)}=\sqrt{24}\text{BM}$

This calculates to approximately 4.89 BM, which rounds to an integer value of 5 BM.

Total number of molecules/species from following which will be paramagnetic is $__________$. 

$\mathrm{O}_{2},\mathrm{O}_{2}^{+},\mathrm{O}_{2}^{-},\mathrm{NO},\mathrm{NO}_{2},\mathrm{CO},\mathrm{K}_{2}[\mathrm{NiCl}_{4}],[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}_{3})_{6}]\mathrm{Cl}_{3},\mathrm{K}_{2}[\mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{CN})_{4}]$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 28th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
To determine which molecules or species are paramagnetic, we need to identify those with unpaired electrons. Here's the analysis:

$\mathrm{O}_{2}$: This molecule has 2 unpaired electrons as predicted by the Molecular Orbital Theory (MOT), making it paramagnetic.

$\mathrm{O}_{2}^{+}$: This ion has 1 unpaired electron according to MOT, which also makes it paramagnetic.

$\mathrm{O}_{2}^{-}$: This ion contains 1 unpaired electron as determined by MOT, indicating it is paramagnetic.

$\mathrm{NO}$: As a species with an odd number of electrons, $\mathrm{NO}$ has unpaired electrons, making it paramagnetic.

$\mathrm{NO}_{2}$: This molecule is also an odd-electron species, which means it has unpaired electrons and is paramagnetic.

$\mathrm{K}_{2}[\mathrm{NiCl}_{4}]$: In this compound, $\mathrm{Ni}^{2+}$ (nickel with a +2 oxidation state) has an electron configuration of $3d^{8}$. Given the presence of weak field ligands and a coordination number of 4, this forms a tetrahedral complex. As a result, it is paramagnetic with 2 unpaired electrons.

Thus, the paramagnetic species in the provided list are $\mathrm{O}_{2}$, $\mathrm{O}_{2}^{+}$, $\mathrm{O}_{2}^{-}$, $\mathrm{NO}$, $\mathrm{NO}_{2}$, and $\mathrm{K}_{2}[\mathrm{NiCl}_{4}]$.

text:
Electrolysis of 600 mL aqueous solution of NaCl for 5 min changes the pH of the solution to 12 .

 The current in Amperes used for the given electrolysis is $___________ . ($Nearest integer).
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 28th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Electrolysis of NaCl is

$\mathrm{NaCl}+\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}(\mathrm{aq})\to \mathrm{NaOH}(\mathrm{aq})+\frac{1}{2}\mathrm{Cl}_{2}(\mathrm{g})+\frac{1}{2}\mathrm{H}_{2}(\mathrm{g})$

Since during electrolysis pH changes to 12

So $\left [\mathrm{OH}^{⊖}\right ]=10^{-2}$ and $[\mathrm{H}^{+}]=10^{-12}$

So by Faraday law

Gram amount of substance deposited $=$
Amount of electricity passed

$\begin{array}{l} 10^{-2}\times \dfrac{600}{1000}\times 96500=\mathrm{I}\times \mathrm{t} \\ \dfrac{10^{-2}\times 600}{1000}\times 96500=\mathrm{I}\times 5\times 60 \\ \mathrm{I}=\dfrac{10^{-2}\times 600\times 96500}{1000\times 5\times 60} \\ \mathrm{I}=1.93\text{ampere} \end{array}$

So, $\mathrm{I}=2$ ampere (nearest integer)

text:
Consider the following data :

Heat of formation of $\mathrm{CO}_{2}(\mathrm{g})=-393.5\mathrm{kJ}\mathrm{mol}{}^{-1}$

Heat of formation of $\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}(\mathrm{l})=-286.0\mathrm{kJ}\mathrm{mol}{}^{-1}$

Heat of combustion of benzene $=-3267.0\mathrm{kJ}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$

The heat of formation of benzene is $__________$ $\mathrm{kJ}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$. (Nearest integer)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 28th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
To determine the heat of formation of benzene ($\Delta H_{f}[\text{C}_{6}\text{H}_{6}]$), we use the given data:

Heat of formation of $\text{CO}_{2}(\text{g})=-393.5\text{kJ/mol}$

Heat of formation of $\text{H}_{2}\text{O}(\text{l})=-286.0\text{kJ/mol}$

Heat of combustion of benzene = $-3267.0\text{kJ/mol}$

The reaction for the combustion of benzene is:

$\text{C}_{6}\text{H}_{6}+\frac{15}{2}\text{O}_{2}(\text{g})\to 6\text{CO}_{2}(\text{g})+3\text{H}_{2}\text{O}(\text{l})$

Using the formula for the enthalpy change of the reaction ($\Delta H_{R}$):

$\Delta H_{R}=\Delta H_{C}=\Sigma \Delta H_{f}(\text{Products})-\Sigma \Delta H_{f}(\text{Reactants})$

Substitute values into the equation:

$-3267=6\times (-393.5)+3\times (-286)-\Delta H_{f}[\text{C}_{6}\text{H}_{6}]$

Solving this equation, we find:

$\Delta H_{f}[\text{C}_{6}\text{H}_{6}]=48\text{kJ/mol}$

Thus, the heat of formation of benzene is $48\text{kJ/mol}$.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 28th January Evening Shift

text:
A group 15 element forms $\mathrm{d}π-\mathrm{d}π$ bond with transition metals. It also forms hydride, which is a strongest base among the hydrides of other group members that form $dπ-dπ$ bond. 

The atomic number of the element is $_______$ .
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 28th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Phosphorus and arsenic form $dπ$–$dπ$ bonds with transition metals when their compounds such as $\mathrm{P}(\mathrm{C}{}_{2}\mathrm{H}{}_{5}){}_{3}$ and $\mathrm{As}(\mathrm{C}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{5}){}_{3}$ act as ligands. Nitrogen cannot, as its valence shell has no $d$ orbitals.

Basicity of group 15 hydrides decreases down the group, because the lone pair occupies a larger, more diffuse orbital:

$\mathrm{NH}{}_{3}>\mathrm{PH}{}_{3}>\mathrm{AsH}{}_{3}>\mathrm{SbH}{}_{3}$

Of the hydrides of P and As, $\mathrm{PH}{}_{3}$ is the stronger base, so the element is phosphorus.

The atomic number of phosphorus is 15 (31 is its atomic mass).

Hence, the answer is 15.
